questions.stem: An infant with X-linked agammaglobulinemia has no infections for the first several months of life and then develops recurrent otitis media and pneumonia. Which of the following best explains this timing?
pearls: Onset before 6 months points toward a severe T-cell or combined defect rather than an isolated antibody defect.
Preterm infants receive less maternal IgG and reach their nadir earlier.

choices.text: Antibodies in breast milk protect the airway until weaning
Neonatal B cells make adequate IgM until 6 months of age
Maternal IgG acquired across the placenta declines after birth
Thymic output is greatest in the first months of life

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.rationale:
**Transplacentally acquired maternal IgG** protects the infant at first. It falls to its lowest level at about 3 to 6 months, and **antibody-deficient infants then become symptomatic**.

| Defect | Onset | Examples |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Combined or T-cell | First weeks to 6 months | SCID, CD40 ligand deficiency |
| Antibody | After 3 to 6 months | X-linked agammaglobulinemia |
| Phagocyte | Early infancy to childhood | Chronic granulomatous disease |
| Complement | Variable, any age | C3 deficiency |

- **Antibodies in breast milk** give mucosal IgA but do not replace systemic IgG.
- **Neonatal B-cell IgM** cannot be made in X-linked agammaglobulinemia because B cells are absent.
- **Thymic output** concerns T cells and does not protect a patient who lacks B cells.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old man drank automotive antifreeze 12 hours ago. He has flank pain, creatinine 3.1 mg/dL (274 µmol/L) and calcium 7.2 mg/dL (1.8 mmol/L). The anion gap is 28 mEq/L. Urine microscopy shows needle- and envelope-shaped crystals. Which of the following best explains his kidney injury?
pearls: Fluorescein in antifreeze makes urine glow under a Wood lamp, but it is an unreliable test.

choices.text: Uric acid crystal obstruction from tumor lysis
Formate toxicity to the renal tubule
Calcium oxalate crystals formed from glycolate

questions.subject: Internal Medicine
questions.rationale:
**Calcium oxalate deposition** explains it. Alcohol dehydrogenase converts ethylene glycol to glycolic acid, which drives the **high anion gap acidosis**, and then to oxalate. Oxalate binds calcium, causing **hypocalcemia**, **calcium oxalate crystals** and tubular injury.

- **Myoglobin casts** need rhabdomyolysis, with a very high creatine kinase and dark urine.
- **Formate** is the toxic metabolite of methanol and injures the optic nerve, not the kidney.
- **Uric acid crystals** occur in tumor lysis and do not cause the hypocalcemia or acidosis here.

Treat with fomepizole. Intermittent hemodialysis is advised for severe features such as coma, seizures or acute kidney injury.

questions.stem: A 28-year-old woman at 36 weeks of gestation with gestational diabetes has a biophysical profile. The ultrasound shows normal breathing, movement and tone, and a single deepest vertical pocket of 4 cm. A nonstress test was not done. How should the result be interpreted?
pearls: The nonstress test is added when any of the four ultrasonographic variables is abnormal.

choices.text: Equivocal, because the missing nonstress test scores 0
Abnormal, because the nonstress test is required for a valid profile
Normal, and the nonstress test can be omitted
Normal, provided it is repeated within 24 hours

questions.subject: Obstetrics & Gynecology
questions.rationale:
**Normal.** The nonstress test can be omitted when all four ultrasonographic components are normal. The score is 8 of 8, which is interpreted as normal and needs no change in management.

- **Equivocal, with the missing test scored 0** is wrong because an omitted component is not scored as abnormal.
- **Abnormal, because the test is required** is wrong because the nonstress test is optional when the four sonographic variables are normal.
- **Normal if repeated in 24 hours** invents a repeat interval. A normal profile is repeated on the usual schedule for the underlying risk.
